title: The boycott ends
hook: some Meccans of conscience tear up the boycott, starting with one man who could no longer eat in peace

segments.voice: Yesterday, bismika Allahumma. Your line was: only the name remained. What did you notice that outlasted everything around it? Day seven hundred forty-seven.

A camel is being led through the dark toward the valley where the Prophet's clan is shut in. It is loaded with food. At the mouth of the valley, Ibn Ishaq tells us, the man leading it takes off its halter, strikes it on the flank, and lets it walk in alone, so nobody can say he broke the agreement. His name is Hisham ibn Amr. He is not one of the Prophet's followers. He is a Meccan with relatives inside, and the agreement sits badly with him. Today: al-sahifa, and it ends because a few people like him stop keeping quiet.
screen: `A CAMEL IN THE DARK.` → `FOOD FOR THE VALLEY.` → `A MAN WITH KIN INSIDE.`

segments.voice: Ibn Ishaq carries it on from there. Hisham goes to a man named Zuhayr, whose mother came from the Prophet's own clan, and asks him a plain question: how can you eat, and dress, and marry, while your mother's family can't buy or sell? Zuhayr answers honestly. What can I do? I'm one man. If I had one more with me, I'd act. So Hisham says: you have one. Me. Zuhayr says, find us another. And Hisham does. He goes to al-Mut'im ibn Adi, then to Abu al-Bakhtari, then to Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, and each time he asks the same question and gets the same answer: not alone. They meet at night above Mecca and agree on a plan. In the morning Zuhayr walks around the Ka'ba and then turns to the crowd and says, in effect: people of Mecca, are we going to eat and wear clothes while this clan perishes? I won't sit down until this unjust, severing document is torn up. Abu Jahl shouts that it will never be torn. And then, one after another, as they planned, the others stand up and say: tear it. Al-Mut'im goes to take the document down, and finds what we heard yesterday: the insects have eaten it, all but the words, in Your name, O Allah. Notice what did the work here. Not an army. Not a miracle alone. A man with food, a question asked out loud, and a promise not to stand by himself. The sirah doesn't present these men as believers in the Prophet's message. It presents them as people who decided a rule was wrong and said so, together. The sirah keeps all five of their names.
screen: `HISHAM ASKS: HOW CAN YOU EAT?` · `ZUHAYR: I'M ONE MAN.` · `ONE BY ONE, THEY JOIN.` · `AT THE KA'BA: TEAR IT UP.` · then, large: `NOT ALONE.`

segments.voice: The practice: speak up against an unfair rule. Sit comfortably and let your breathing slow. Bring to mind one rule, or one habit of a group you're in, that lands hard on someone who can't easily push back. A workplace policy. A family pattern. A rule at school. Don't fix it yet. Just see it clearly. Then do what Hisham did: name one person who might stand up with you. Picture asking them. And then shape one sentence you could say out loud, short and fair, the way Zuhayr did at the Ka'ba. Some who pray ask Allah here for the courage to say it. The bell holds the time.
Al-sahifa, the written document. In Ibn Ishaq's telling, a handful of Meccans agree one by one, stand up at the Ka'ba, and it comes down. Today's word.
Your line: conscience ended it. Today, say your one fair sentence to one person, or find the one person who'll stand with you when you do. Day seven hundred forty-seven.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the end of the boycott as part of the Meccan sirah, and the names of the Meccans who worked to end it are kept in Ibn Ishaq's account and retold in sirah study.

fork.setup: you're Zuhayr. a friend asks how you can eat while your relatives starve. you know you can't change it alone. what do you say?
options: nothing can be done. let it go.
find me one more, and I'll act.
I'll go to the Ka'ba alone right now.
fork.reveal: Ibn Ishaq says Zuhayr asked for one more. Hisham named himself, then went and found others.

original.note: Arabic: the written page or document; the sirah calls the boycott agreement al-sahifa.

trapdoor: what you thought: the boycott just faded away.
what it means: a few Meccans of conscience agreed together and stood up in public.
what a scholar hears: Ibn Ishaq names Hisham, Zuhayr, al-Mut'im, Abu al-Bakhtari and Zam'a, and joins their stand to the eaten document.

sources.ref: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (the annulment of the boycott: Hisham ibn Amr, Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayya, al-Mut'im ibn Adi, Abu al-Bakhtari, Zam'a ibn al-Aswad; the document eaten except 'bismika Allahumma')

notes: All story details (the camel sent in with its halter removed, Zuhayr's mother from Banu Hashim/Abd al-Muttalib, the order of recruitment, the night meeting, Zuhayr's words at the Ka'ba, Abu Jahl's objection, al-Mut'im going to the document) are paraphrased from Ibn Ishaq as recalled; confirm against the sirah.
Zuhayr's speech is paraphrased ('in effect'); no translation is quoted.
'The sirah doesn't present these men as believers in the Prophet's message' is a general characterization; confirm it is fair for all five named.
